Subject: Renewal planning: target dates and options

Hi Martin,

We’re starting the renewal discussion for Concourse’s annual plan that comes up 11/15. Quick context: your team’s 12-month average consumption has grown ~38% QoQ (thanks for sending the usage files). Given that growth, there are a few ways we can structure the renewal to keep unit economics predictable for you while preserving flexibility for spikes.

Options I recommend we discuss on a short call (30m):
- Option A: 12-month fixed commit at a 15% effective discount, 10% one-time onboarding credit to offset Q4 overages.
- Option B: 9-month ramped commit (50% first 3 months, 75% next 3, then full) with a 12% discount and a smaller $15k credit that vests after month 3.
- Option C: Pay-as-you-go with a 5% volume rebate quarterly (best for unpredictable spikes).

Two asks from me before we sync: can you confirm expected average Q1 volume if you proceed with an aggressive upsell (ballpark is fine), and whether procurement needs a standing PO vs a signed addendum? I’ve attached the usage snapshot you sent plus a sketch term sheet (see Concourse_Renewal_Redline_v3.pdf stub).

Would Tuesday 10/10 10:00 PT work for a 30m? If not, propose two times and I’ll coordinate.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee

Subject: RE: Renewal planning: target dates and options — Pricing sketch

Martin — appreciated the details. Based on the +60% uplift and procurement needing a PO, here’s a pragmatic sketch we can firm up on the 10/10 call:

Proposal (sketch):
- Term: 12 months (start on renewal effective date).
- Commit: 9-month ramped commit (50% / 75% / 100%) applied to baseline tokens; overage billed at committed unit rate until the 9-month mark, then standard agreed rate.
- Effective discount: 13% off list on committed volume.
- One-time front-loaded credit: $40,000 applied to the first invoice (covers December overage risk).
- Price hold: 6 months on per-token list price after go-live (Redwood will not increase the per-token list price for 6 months).
- Procurement flow: sign addendum + PO; we’ll issue invoice per the addendum schedule.

Notes: The $40k credit is front-loaded because Concourse is bringing a sizeable uplift and we want to remove the December spike risk. The discount level balances predictability and our margin profile given the ramp. If you need a larger credit in exchange for a higher commit, we can discuss a stepped credit tied to a higher floor.

I’ll bring a tightened term sheet with exact phrasing for the price-hold clause and billing schedule to the call.

Best,
Ben Carter
